text.p: These are the leading stories in the Zimbabwe press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The International Monetary Fund, which summarily withdrew its credit support for Zimbabwe's economic reform programme two years ago, will consider resuming funding after the presentation of the southern African country's 18-month budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year in July.
- State-owned airliner Air Zimbabwe is bankrupt and cannot meet all its obligations, acting managing director Peter Chikumba has admitted in a detailed financial report.
- The Zimbabwe Independent goes on-line this week, becoming the country's first national newspaper to appear on the Internet.

- Telecel International, working with a consortium of Zimbabwean organisations and individuals, will over the next four years invest more than Z$1.5 billion during the implementation stages of the country's second cellular phone network scheduled to be operational by September.

- Disciplinary charges against suspended Zimbabwe National Parks director Willie Nduku and his deputy Rowan Martin arose out of attempts to discredit and so eliminate the pair so that others could exercise the discretionary powers of the Parks directorate, their lawyers claim.
